title: The Incident of the Disputed Inheritance
text: You discover that your late uncle's estate—comprising three fine horses, a small vineyard, and a collection of antique swords—has been claimed by a distant cousin who presents documents of questionable authenticity. The local magistrate appears disinclined to intervene. How do you proceed?
choices: Challenge the cousin to a duel at dawn, for honor demands satisfaction and the matter shall be settled by steel
Hire an advocate well-versed in Imperial law and pursue the matter through every available court, however long it may take
Arrange a private meeting with the cousin to negotiate a settlement that benefits both parties, perhaps over wine

title: The Matter of the Overheard Conspiracy
text: While dining at a reputable establishment, you overhear two nobles at the adjacent table discussing what appears to be a plot to embarrass a high-ranking official at the upcoming Imperial Ball. The matter does not directly concern you, yet you possess information that could prevent scandal.
choices: Immediately report what you have heard to the proper authorities, as duty demands
Investigate the matter further on your own, gathering evidence before deciding on a course of action
Mind your own affairs entirely, as the schemes of others are not your concern unless they directly threaten you or yours

title: The Predicament of the Borrowed Gold
text: A friend of long standing requests a substantial loan to cover a gambling debt that, if unpaid, will result in significant social embarrassment. You have the funds available, though lending them would require delaying your own planned renovations to your country estate.
choices: Lend the full amount without hesitation, for friendship and loyalty transcend mere financial considerations
Offer to lend a portion while helping your friend negotiate better terms with the creditor
Politely decline, suggesting instead that your friend face the consequences and learn from this experience

title: The Affair of the Artistic Commission
text: You have commissioned a portrait from a renowned artist. Upon completion, you find the work technically masterful but discover the artist has taken considerable creative liberty, depicting you in a manner that, while flattering, bears little resemblance to your actual appearance or character.
choices: Accept the portrait graciously and display it prominently, for art serves a higher truth than mere physical accuracy
Request that the artist revise the work to achieve a more accurate representation, as truth in all things is paramount
Pay for the work but decline to display it, commissioning a different artist who will follow your specifications precisely

title: The Incident at the Mountain Pass
text: While traveling through a remote mountain pass, your party encounters a group of bandits demanding a toll for safe passage. You outnumber them, but conflict would likely result in casualties on both sides. The bandits appear desperate rather than professional criminals.
choices: Refuse to pay and prepare for battle, for yielding to extortion sets a dangerous precedent
Negotiate a reduced toll while making note of their faces to report them to authorities at your destination
Pay the toll without complaint and continue on your way, as your time and safety are worth more than gold

title: The Mystery of the Anonymou Gift
text: You receive an expensive gift—a finely crafted dagger of obvious quality—with no indication of the sender. Inquiries among your acquaintances yield no answers, and the merchant who delivered it claims ignorance of the patron's identity, having been paid by an intermediary.
choices: Keep the weapon and remain alert, for such a gift likely carries obligations or dangers that will reveal themselves in time
Conduct a thorough investigation to determine the sender's identity before deciding whether to keep or return the gift
Return the gift to the merchant and refuse all anonymous presents, as accepting obligations to unknown parties is unwise

title: The Question of the Imprudent Servant
text: Your most trusted servant, in your employ for fifteen years, has been discovered stealing small amounts of wine from your cellar—not for sale, but for personal consumption. The quantities are negligible, but the principle of theft has been violated.
choices: Dismiss the servant immediately and publicly, for trust once broken cannot be restored and examples must be set
Reprimand the servant severely and dock their wages for the value stolen, but maintain their employment
Have a private conversation to understand their motivations, then decide based on their explanation and your assessment of their character

title: The Dilemma of the Political Alliance
text: A powerful noble offers an advantageous political alliance that would significantly advance your family's standing at court. However, this noble is known for holding views on Imperial policy that directly contradict your own deeply-held convictions regarding the treatment of Eastern provinces.
choices: Accept the alliance, for political advantage should not be sacrificed for abstract principles when real power is at stake
Decline politely but firmly, as compromising one's fundamental beliefs for advancement is the path to dishonor
Accept the alliance while privately working to moderate the noble's views or to limit their influence on related policies

title: The Circumstance of the Challenged Duel
text: You have been challenged to a duel by a hot-headed young noble over a perceived slight that was, in truth, entirely unintentional on your part. The challenger is known to be an excellent swordsman, though inexperienced in actual combat. Refusing would damage your reputation, but you have no desire to kill or be killed over a misunderstanding.
choices: Accept the duel without hesitation, for honor demands it, and trust in your own skill and the gods to determine the outcome
Attempt to resolve the misunderstanding through intermediaries, offering a formal apology to avoid bloodshed
Accept the duel but plan to disarm rather than kill your opponent, demonstrating both courage and mercy

title: The Problem of the Failing Enterprise
text: A business venture in which you have invested substantially is failing due to circumstances beyond anyone's control—poor weather has destroyed harvests for two consecutive years. Your partners wish to continue, requesting additional investment, but advisors suggest cutting losses and withdrawing.
choices: Invest additional funds and remain committed to the enterprise, for loyalty to one's partners and persistence in adversity define character
Withdraw your investment immediately to minimize losses, as sentiment has no place in financial decisions
Propose restructuring the venture under new terms that distribute risk more equitably before committing further funds

title: The Situation of the Forbidden Knowledge
text: Through circumstances of pure chance, you have come into possession of a book containing sorcerous techniques that, while not explicitly illegal, are considered dangerous and are certainly frowned upon by the Empire. The knowledge within is fascinating and potentially valuable.
choices: Study the book thoroughly, for knowledge itself is neither good nor evil, and understanding such techniques may prove useful
Turn the book over to Imperial authorities immediately, as possessing such knowledge invites both danger and suspicion
Consult with a discreet expert in such matters before deciding, gathering more information about the actual risks involved

title: The Incident of the Public Humiliation
text: At a well-attended social gathering, a rival makes several cutting remarks about your family's recent financial difficulties. The comments, while within the bounds of propriety, are clearly intended to embarrass you before your peers. Several people are watching to see how you respond.
choices: Respond with equally sharp wit, turning the embarrassment back upon your rival in a manner that demonstrates your verbal superiority
Maintain perfect composure and courtesy, refusing to acknowledge the slight and thereby demonstrating that such petty attacks cannot affect you
Challenge the rival to a duel, for such calculated disrespect to one's family cannot be tolerated regardless of social setting

title: The Matter of the Strategic Betrayal
text: You have learned that an ally is planning to betray your mutual patron in a scheme that, while dishonorable, would likely succeed and benefit all participants except the patron. Your ally approaches you to join the conspiracy, offering substantial rewards and suggesting the patron has grown weak and ineffective.
choices: Join the conspiracy, for when circumstances change, alliances must adapt, and loyalty to a failing cause is mere stubbornness
Refuse participation and warn your patron immediately, as betrayal is betrayal regardless of potential benefits
Refuse to participate but remain silent about the conspiracy, allowing events to unfold without your involvement

title: The Question of the Experimental Method
text: You have an opportunity to participate in a sorcerous experiment that could significantly advance understanding of the Orb's nature. However, the experiment carries substantial personal risk, and the researcher leading it acknowledges that the probability of success is uncertain at best.
choices: Volunteer eagerly, for the advancement of knowledge and the glory of potential discovery far outweigh personal danger
Decline participation, as risking one's life for uncertain theoretical gains demonstrates poor judgment
Offer to assist with the experiment in a supporting role that minimizes personal risk while still contributing to the work

title: The Dilemma of the Unjust Law
text: A new Imperial decree, perfectly legal and properly promulgated, requires actions that you find morally unconscionable—specifically, the increased taxation of Eastern merchants in a manner you believe constitutes unjust persecution. Compliance is mandatory, and non-compliance would result in severe penalties.
choices: Comply with the law while working through proper channels to have it revised or repealed, for the law must be obeyed even when unjust
Refuse to comply and accept whatever penalties result, for conscience must take precedence over law when they conflict
Find creative ways to technically comply with the letter of the law while subverting its intent, protecting those you believe are unjustly targeted

title: The Circumstance of the Collapsing Bridge
text: While crossing a bridge with a group of travelers, you notice alarming structural damage that suggests imminent collapse. There is time for most to cross, but you are at the rear of the group. Warning everyone might cause a panic that ensures the bridge's collapse, while remaining silent would allow those ahead to cross safely but might doom those behind.
choices: Shout a clear warning immediately, for everyone deserves knowledge of the danger even if panic results
Quickly but calmly organize an orderly crossing, using your authority to prevent panic while expediting passage
Ensure you cross to safety first, then warn those behind, for you cannot help others if you perish in the collapse

title: The Affair of the Discovered Treasure
text: While exploring ruins on your estate, you discover a cache of ancient treasures—coins, jewelry, and artifacts of considerable historical value. By law, such finds must be reported to Imperial authorities, who will claim a substantial portion. However, the discovery was made on your land, and no one else knows of it.
choices: Report the find immediately and completely, for the law is the law and your honor requires compliance regardless of personal cost
Keep the discovery secret and dispose of the items through private channels, for what is found on your land is rightfully yours
Report a portion of the find while keeping the most valuable items, satisfying legal requirements while protecting your interests
